judgments.notes: Occupation matches exactly: qualified carpenter, trade certificate, permanent full-time, and the seeker's category B licence satisfies the stated "Kørekort B" requirement. Graded 2 rather than 3 because the ad adds a specialism the seeker never mentions — knowledge or practical experience of the glazing trade is listed as a firm requirement ("Du har kendskab til eller praktisk erfaring med glarmesterfaget"), not a nice-to-have — and it also requires willingness to relocate to Lolland, Denmark and settle there, which the seeker has not expressed. Uncertainty resolved downward per instructions. On task two: the ad requires the legal right to work in Denmark (EU/EEA, Swiss or a Danish permit); the seeker said nothing about citizenship or work authorisation, so this cannot be scored as a violation of something they explicitly lack. Language requirement is "You can communicate in English", which the seeker's statement is consistent with; the ad never requires Norwegian, and the seeker's lack of Norwegian is irrelevant here since the workplace is Danish and no Danish requirement is stated. The Danish-language duplicate section is merely a translation of the same posting, not a requirement on the applicant.

judgments.constraint_evidence: Må kunne kommunisere på norsk
judgments.notes: Occupation and level match squarely: warehouse work plus forklift driving, and the required truckførerbevis is held by the seeker. Experience from a warehouse is only "en fordel", so its absence does not lower the grade. Ignoring language, this is exactly the job sought — grade 3. Separately, the ad explicitly requires ability to communicate in Norwegian, which the seeker says they cannot yet do; this is a stated language requirement in the ad text, not an inference from silence, so it is a violation. A grade 3 match the seeker cannot currently take.

Seeker is a nurse with hospital and nursing-home experience seeking a permanent day-shift position. The advertisement is for a waiter/server as extra help (food serving, cleaning, dishwashing, till work) on call at short notice — a different occupation entirely, and also the opposite contract type. Grade 0.

Task two: the ad requires fluent Norwegian ("Vi ser etter deg som snakker flytende norsk og som er effektiv"), but the seeker explicitly states she speaks fluent Norwegian, so this is satisfied, not violated. No authorisation or licence requirement is stated. No violation.

The advertisement is for a service worker (servicemedarbeider) cleaning/checking public toilets for JCDecaux — a cleaning/facilities occupation entirely different from nursing. No clinical or care duties, no health qualifications sought; the only hard requirement is a class B driving licence and physical fitness. Grade 0 for irrelevant occupation. It also conflicts with the seeker's shift preference (work every other weekend rather than day shifts), but that is secondary to the occupational mismatch. Task two: Norwegian is listed only under "Ønskede kvalifikasjoner" (desired, not essential) — "Gode norsk kunnskaper, skriftlig og muntlig" — so it is not a hard requirement and no violation is recorded. The class B licence is an essential requirement, but the seeker said nothing about lacking a driving licence, so that is not a violation of anything she explicitly stated.

The seeker is a data scientist seeking AI/analytics roles with ML, Python and SQL. This is a Growth Engineer role: a full-stack/frontend software engineering position focused on building user-facing web app features, onboarding flows, landing pages and growth infrastructure. The minimum requirements demand strong frontend skills, 3+ years shipping user-facing web applications, and experience with APIs/backends — none of which the seeker claims. There is partial overlap (analytics, event tracking, experimentation, data work, AI tooling), so it is adjacent rather than irrelevant, but this is a different occupation from data science/AI and the seeker would not apply. Graded down rather than 2 per the instruction to record the lower grade when uncertain.

Task two: the advertisement says nothing about requiring Norwegian language; it states "Since English is widely spoken, international talent can easily settle in and feel at home," which is the opposite of a Norwegian requirement. The clause "We prioritize candidates that are either are already located in Oslo, or who have an existing right to work in Norway and are willing to relocate to Oslo" is a stated prioritisation preference about location/work authorisation, and the seeker said nothing about lacking a right to work in Norway — the only thing they explicitly said they lack is Norwegian, which this ad does not require. Therefore no violation of anything the seeker explicitly said they do not have.

The post is for a teacher at grades 1-4 (primary level), which matches a qualified primary school teacher seeking work in Norway exactly — right occupation, right level, so grade 3 ignoring language. Task two: the advertisement body is empty (only empty section headings: Arbeidsoppgaver, Kvalifikasjoner, Vi tilbyr, etc.), so there is no stated requirement of any kind. No language requirement, no authorisation requirement, no licence requirement is expressed in the text. Per rule 1, silence is not a violation — the Norwegian title and Norwegian headings are not evidence of an imposed language requirement. Recorded as no violation on the available text.

Right occupation and level: sykepleier with experience from hospital and municipal care, which matches the ad's "Erfaring fra primær- eller spesialisthelsetjenesten". However the contract type is off: this is agency/locum travel work via a staffing bureau (Dedicare), where you choose short periods, travel and live in provided housing, and shifts are wherever needed across the country — the seeker explicitly wants a "fast stilling" and preferably day shifts. No permanent position or day-shift arrangement is offered, and flexibility/travel willingness is an explicit qualification. Graded 2 (right field, wrong contract type) rather than 3; uncertainty resolved downward. Task two: the ad requires "Beherske et nordisk språk flytende, både muntlig og skriftlig" — the seeker states she speaks fluent Norwegian, so this is satisfied, not violated. No authorisation or licence requirement is stated that she lacks.

judgments.constraint_evidence: Gode norsk kunnskaper, skriftlig og muntlig
judgments.notes: The seeker wants warehouse work and holds a forklift certificate. This is a service/cleaning role (toilet checking and washing) for JCDecaux, a different occupation entirely — no warehouse, logistics or forklift element at all, so grade 0. The role also requires a class B driving licence, which the seeker does not mention, but they did not explicitly say they lack it, so that is not recorded as a violation. Language: the ad lists "Gode norsk kunnskaper, skriftlig og muntlig" under desired (ønskede) rather than essential qualifications; it is recorded as a language violation because the seeker explicitly states they do not speak Norwegian, though its placement among preferred qualifications makes this weaker than a hard bar.

judgments.constraint_evidence: Fluency in Norwegian and English, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
judgments.notes: This is a field-based commercial sales role (Territory Manager) requiring a bachelor's degree plus sales/account management experience in medical devices, with frequent travel and responsibility for sales targets, tenders and pricing. The seeker is a clinical nurse seeking a permanent, preferably day-shift nursing position. Although the role touches the healthcare sector and involves engaging with hospital clinicians, it is a different occupation entirely — sales rather than patient care — and the seeker's stated wish for day shifts and nursing work does not align. Grade 0 rather than 1 because none of the seeker's actual nursing duties are performed here; the only overlap is the hospital setting. Separately, the advertisement explicitly requires fluency in Norwegian, which the seeker states they do not have — a clear language violation (not merely inferred from the Norwegian section headings such as "Hva vi ser etter" or "Arbeidsoppgaver"). A valid driver's licence is also required but the seeker said nothing about lacking one, so that is not recorded as a violation.

Seeker is a backend developer (Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes) wanting a permanent role in Oslo or hybrid. The ad is for an experienced tile setter (flislegger) on new-build bathrooms — an entirely different occupation with no overlap in skills or sector, hence grade 0. The location requirement ("Du må bo i Trondheimsområdet") conflicts with the seeker's Oslo/hybrid preference, but location is a preference mismatch, not one of the stated violation facets (language, authorisation, licence). The ad states no language, authorisation or licence requirement; the seeker speaks Norwegian in any case, so no violation is recorded.

Occupation matches (senior backend developer, permanent-looking consultancy/customer role, flexible workday consistent with hybrid Oslo). However the core technical stack is off: required qualifications centre on C# .NET and Azure-specific services (Entra, Key Vault, App Services, Azure Functions) plus CIAM, none of which the seeker mentions. The seeker's Python and PostgreSQL only partially align ("Relational Database (SQL)"), and Kubernetes appears merely among desired, not required, qualifications. A Python backend developer would not apply to a C# .NET role as written, so this is adjacent rather than plausible; graded down from 2 to 1 because the mandatory stack, not just the level or specialism, is mismatched. Task two: the advertisement is written in Norwegian but states no language requirement anywhere — silence is not a violation, and no authorisation or licence is demanded either.

Right occupation (carpenter) and the seeker has a trade certificate plus ten years' experience, matching the "vocational school" requirement comfortably. However, the specialism is off: this is ship interior outfitting at a shipyard, requiring knowledge of ship interior build, bathroom module installation, wall/ceiling panel systems and furniture installation, on a 4:2 rotation. The seeker's background is new builds and renovation in building construction, not marine outfitting, and no furniture-installation experience is stated. Graded 2 rather than 3 because of that specialism and contract-type mismatch; the transferable carpentry skills are real but the advertisement as written asks for ship-interior knowledge the seeker does not claim.

Task two: no violation. Language requirement is "Minimum level of spoken English" — English, not Norwegian — so the seeker's lack of Norwegian is not in conflict; the advertisement is silent on Norwegian. The background check / security clearance by the Norwegian National Security Authority is a vetting step, not a licence or authorisation the seeker said they lack. Driving licence is not mentioned, and the seeker holds category B in any case.

Seeker is a data scientist with ML, Python and SQL experience looking for a role in AI or analysis. This is a three-year PhD fellowship (stipendiat) at NIBIO/NMBU — a research training contract, not an industry data science/analyst position. Shared technical ground exists (machine learning, Python, deep learning), but the specialism is highly specific: 3D LiDAR point clouds, robotics, SLAM, real-time embedded inference, plus mandatory fieldwork in Norwegian forests. Explicit eligibility bars (no prior doctorate, no prior stipendiat position) and a required master's in computer science/ML/robotics further narrow it. The seeker did not express interest in a doctoral track. Adjacent rather than plausible: grade 1 chosen over 2 because the contract type, research-training level and robotics/forestry specialism all diverge, and the uncertainty rule says record the lower grade. Language: the ad requires good English, and asks only that applicants who cannot document Norwegian/Swedish/Danish at A2 accept free Norwegian training — the seeker states "Jeg snakker norsk", so nothing is violated. Norwegian is listed only as an advantage ("Kunnskaper i norsk eller et annet skandinavisk språk"). No authorisation or licence requirement is imposed.

Bred konsulentutlysning (Folk AS) som blant annet nevner "Data engineering, analyse og dataplattformer" og "AI, maskinlæring og generativ AI", samt Python — dette overlapper klart med søkerens kompetanse innen maskinlæring, Python og SQL, og med ønsket om stilling innen AI eller analyse. Graderes likevel 2, ikke 3: annonsen er rettet mot utvikler/arkitekt/data engineer/teknologirådgiver snarere enn data scientist, den er en generell kandidatinnsamling til konsulentoppdrag (kontraktstype/rolle er uspesifisert), og den krever minimum 3-5 års relevant erfaring, noe søkeren ikke dokumenterer. Usikkerheten løses nedover som instruert. Språk: annonsen krever "Flytende Norsk, både muntlig og skriftlig", men søkeren oppgir selv at hun snakker norsk, så dette er ikke et brudd.

Right field (AI/ML) and overlapping skills (Python, SQL, machine learning/deep learning), but the role is explicitly full-stack: it requires backend C#, frontend JavaScript/React, API/integration design, build and deploy pipelines, and end-to-end software ownership. The seeker describes themselves as a data scientist seeking AI or analytics work, not a full-stack engineer, so the specialism is off — grade 2 rather than 3. Graded down on uncertainty since the ML core is a genuine fit but the advertised requirements as written extend well beyond the seeker's stated skills. On language: the advertisement requires fluent English (which the seeker has) and states only that "Working knowledge of Norwegian is an advantage" — an advantage, not a requirement, so no violation. No authorisation or licence requirement is mentioned.

Different occupation entirely: an on-call ("ringevikar") physical labour/helper role, ~10 hrs/week part-time, suited to students. The seeker is a backend developer (Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes) seeking a permanent role — no overlap in occupation, field, or contract type. Only the Oslo location matches, which is not enough for grade 1. On language: the advertisement is written in Norwegian but states no explicit language requirement anywhere in the text, and silence is not a violation, so no language violation is recorded. No authorisation or licence requirement is stated either.

Right field: carpentry in construction, and the seeker has a trade certificate plus ten years in new builds and renovation, which the ad explicitly values ("Relevant trade certificate or equivalent experience in roofing/carpentry"). However the role as written is primarily a taktekker (roofer) position — the core requirements are roofing installation, insulation, waterproofing and working at height, with carpentry only as it relates to roof structures and fascia boards. The seeker describes general carpentry, not roofing specialism, so the specialism is off; graded 2 rather than 3, and the lower grade chosen deliberately despite the employer's "What you don't have we will provide or learn you!", since flexibility is not the same as a match as advertised. Task two: language is mentioned only as "Basic communication skills in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language, and a valid driver's license (class B) are beneficial." — "beneficial" is a preference, not a requirement, so the lack of Norwegian is not a violation. The class B licence is held in any case, and no authorisation or additional licence is demanded (working-at-height certification is qualified with "where required" and the employer offers to provide training).

Seeker is a backend developer (Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes) wanting a permanent role in Oslo or hybrid. The ad is for a concrete worker (betongfagarbeider/BAS) on construction projects in Trondheim, requiring a fagbrev in the concrete trade. Entirely different occupation, different sector, different location — grade 0. On task two: the ad requires Norwegian ("Må kunne beherske norsk og gjerne polsk språk"), but the seeker states they speak Norwegian, so no language violation. The fagbrev requirement is a trade certificate the seeker did not explicitly say they lack; they simply described a different profession, so it is captured in the grade rather than recorded as a stated-missing credential.

Occupation is an exact match: warehouse/logistics forklift driver work, shift-like hours (07:00-22:00), truckførerbevis required and the seeker has it, plus driving licence noted as an advantage. However, the location is Lillestrøm/Fetsund (eastern Norway), while the seeker explicitly seeks work in Bergen — roughly 500 km away, so this person would not apply. Graded 1 (adjacent: right field and skills, wrong geography) rather than 2, taking the lower grade as instructed since location is stated as a firm part of the posting. On task two: the ad only asks for T1/T2/T4 truckførerbevis (which the seeker has, unspecified classes — no stated lack) and says "Snakker norsk eller engelsk", which is a choice of either language and no violation for a Norwegian-speaking seeker. No requirement the seeker said they lack.

Right occupation (sykepleier) and the seeker has the required norsk autorisasjon/HPR, so the licence requirement is satisfied. However the contract type is off: this is agency/locum work ("oppdrag") of shorter and longer duration, with emphasis on flexibility and travelling to various places in Norway, while the seeker explicitly wants a fast stilling (permanent post) in Trondheim, preferably day shifts. No specific location is named and Trondheim is not mentioned, and no fixed shift pattern is offered. Grade 2 rather than 3 because of the contract-type and location/shift mismatch; not 1 because the occupation and field are exactly right and assignments could in principle be in Trøndelag. Task two: the only requirement stated is norsk autorisasjon som sykepleier, which the seeker has; the ad says nothing about language proficiency, so no violation (silence is not a violation).

The post is for a helsefagarbeider (auxiliary/health care worker with fagbrev), a lower qualification level than a nurse (sykepleier). Same sector and clinical setting (hospital-style sengepost with rehabilitation and ØHD beds, nursing-home-adjacent work), and the ad does add "Andre med helsefaglig bakgrunn er også velkomne til å søke", but grading as written: this is not the occupation or level the seeker holds, so it is adjacent rather than plausible — a nurse would not normally apply for a helsefagarbeider post. Also off on two of the seeker's own wants: the position is 64.2 % part-time rather than full, and the rota explicitly includes "arbeid hver fjerde helg", so not day shifts only. It is a fast (permanent) stilling, which matches. Graded down to 1 per the instruction to take the lower grade where uncertain — the "other health backgrounds welcome" line is employer flexibility, which the instructions say does not raise the grade. Task two: the advertisement says nothing whatsoever about language requirements, Norwegian or otherwise, and does not mention norsk autorisasjon — only "fagbrev som autorisert helsefagarbeider, eller autorisert hjelpepleier", which is a qualification the seeker's nursing credential does not bear on in the facets she named. Silence is not a violation, so no violation recorded.

judgments.constraint_evidence: Gode norskkunnskaper, både skriftlig og muntlig, forutsettes.
judgments.notes: The seeker is a nurse with hospital and nursing-home experience seeking a permanent position, preferably day shifts. This advertisement is for a medical secretary (helsesekretær) at a GP office — a different occupation within the health sector, administrative/reception rather than nursing. Contract type matches (fast stilling, 80%, daytime clinic hours), and some clinical tasks (lab/EKG/spirometri, skiftestue) overlap slightly with nursing, but the role is clerical and the ad prioritises prior legekontor experience, not nursing. A nurse would not normally apply for this. Graded 1 rather than 2 because the occupation itself is different, and the lower grade is recorded where uncertain. Language: the ad explicitly requires good Norwegian in writing and speech, which the seeker says she does not have — a genuine language violation quoted verbatim.

The seeker wants warehouse work and holds a forklift certificate. The advertisement is for a furniture/interior carpenter and CNC operator (plus a paint-shop lacquerer) in a joinery workshop, with a desired trade certificate (fagbrev) in furniture carpentry. That is a different occupation entirely — skilled woodworking/production craft rather than warehouse/logistics work — so grade 0. Assembly and finishing work is mentioned, but nothing warehouse- or forklift-related, so not even adjacent in the seeker's terms.

Task two: the advertisement states "Snakker og skriver norsk evt engelsk", i.e. Norwegian or alternatively English. Per rule 3 this is a choice of either language, and the seeker (writing in English and only stating a lack of Norwegian) is not excluded by it. No violation recorded. The fagbrev wish is expressed as a preference with experience as an acceptable substitute, and the seeker did not say they lack it, so no licence violation either.

Seeker is a certified carpenter (fagbrev) with ten years' experience in both new build and rehabilitation; the ad seeks exactly that — fagbrev som tømrer, erfaring fra nybygg og/eller rehabilitering — with both permanent and project contracts offered, so contract type is not a mismatch. Right occupation and right level: grade 3. Task two: the only requirements stated are Norwegian/Scandinavian language (seeker speaks Norwegian), fagbrev (has it), and class B licence as an advantage (has it). Nothing required that the seeker said they lack.

Field overlap is real: data/analyse/ML, Python, SQL, Databricks, and the seeker wants AI/analysis work. But the ad is a graduate programme strictly reserved for candidates who complete a master's degree in spring 2027 ("For å være aktuell for opptak i tech graduate-programmet må du fullføre en masterutdanning ... i løpet av våren 2027"), with start August 2027, and the role is data engineer rather than data scientist. The seeker presents as an experienced data scientist, so as written they are not eligible and would not apply — adjacent, grade 1. Graded down rather than 2 because the eligibility window is an explicit hard gate on level/status, not merely a preference. Task two: the ad does require Norwegian ("Du må kunne formulere deg godt på norsk, både muntlig og skriftlig"), but the seeker states "Jeg snakker norsk", so no facet they said they lack is required. No authorisation or licence requirement. Background check and ID check are not facets the seeker disclaimed.

The advertisement seeks formwork carpenters and steel fixers (forskalingssnekkere/jernbindere) for construction projects, requiring 3-5 years documented trade experience. The seeker is a backend software developer (Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes). Entirely different occupation with no overlap in skills or sector, so grade 0. Location (Oslo/Østlandet) matches but that is incidental. On language: the ad states "Kommuniserer godt på enten Norsk eller Engelsk" — an either/or choice, so English alone satisfies it; per rule 3 this is not a violation. No authorisation or licence requirement stated.

The seeker is a carpenter with a trade certificate and ten years in new builds and renovation; this advertisement is for a van driver with a tail lift, carrying household goods for customers — a different occupation. It is adjacent only in that it is manual work and uses the category B licence the seeker holds, and training is offered, but a qualified carpenter would not be applying for this. Graded 1 rather than 2 because there is no overlap in the trade itself. Task two: the advertisement says nothing whatever about language — the only stated conditions are a class B licence (which the seeker holds) and residence in Oslo (the seeker said nothing about residence, so this is not something they explicitly said they lack). The Norwegian-plus-English duplication of the residence line is a translation, not a language requirement. No violation on the evidence in the text; inferring one from the fact that the posting is in Norwegian would be exactly the silence error.

Right occupation (nursing) and the post is permanent ("fast stilling"), which matches the seeker's wish. However it is graded down to 2 because: (a) it asks for an "Autorisert spesialsykepleier barn" — a paediatric specialist nurse qualification the seeker does not claim, her experience being hospital and nursing-home general nursing; (b) it is 75% rather than full-time; and (c) it is explicitly a rotating shift post — "Stillingen er turnusstilling, med arbeid på dag, kveld, natt og helg" — contrary to her preference for day shifts. The ad does allow that "søkere med erfaring fra våre fagområder kan vurderes" if no qualified specialists apply, but that is employer flexibility rather than the job as written, so I do not lift the grade for it. Uncertainty between 2 and 3 resolved downward for the specialism and shift mismatch.

Task two: the advertisement text says nothing whatsoever about language skills, Norwegian proficiency, or the language of the application. It does not mention "norsk autorisasjon" either — only "Autorisert spesialsykepleier barn", which is a licence/specialism matter and in any case not something the seeker explicitly said she lacks (she states she is a nurse; she does not state she lacks Norwegian authorisation). The advertisement being written in Norwegian is not itself a requirement. Per the silence rule, no violation is recorded.

Right occupation (sykepleier), right location (Trondheim) and right contract type (fast 100 % stilling), and the seeker's norsk autorisasjon matches the only hard qualification. However the seeker explicitly wants day shifts, while the ad is built around 12.5-hour long weekend shifts and states as a personal requirement "Trives med å jobbe i turnus med både dag og kveldsvakter." That shift pattern conflicts with the stated preference, so the level/contract fit is off rather than squarely what she is looking for — graded 2 as the lower of 2/3 given the uncertainty about how binding the turnus expectation is. No language requirement is stated anywhere in the ad; "Norsk autorisasjon som sykepleier" is a licence requirement which she holds, so no violation.

judgments.constraint_evidence: har erfaring med å undervise norsk som andrespråk for voksne
judgments.notes: Teaching occupation, so the sector overlaps, but this is adult vocational/corporate Norwegian-as-a-second-language instruction on a freelance/oppdrag basis (ENK, self-employed), not primary school teaching. Wrong level (adults, not children), wrong specialism (Norwegian language instruction) and wrong contract type, so grade 1 rather than 2; the seeker as a primary teacher would not apply. Task two: the job's core subject matter is teaching Norwegian as a second language, and the requirement for experience teaching norsk som andrespråk presupposes Norwegian proficiency the seeker explicitly says she lacks — this is an explicit textual requirement, not inferred from the advert being written in Norwegian.

Seeker is a data scientist with machine learning, Python and SQL experience seeking AI/analytics roles. The ad is a 3-year PhD fellowship (stipendiat) in climate data analysis and ML-based emulation of hydrological models: the technical core (Python, neural networks, PyTorch, large-scale data analysis) overlaps well, but the level and contract type are off — it is a doctoral research-training position requiring a master's in data science, atmospheric science, meteorology or hydrology plus domain-specific experience (hydrological modelling, climate data in NetCDF, Unix/Linux), not an industry AI/analyst role. Graded 2 rather than 3 because of the level/contract mismatch and the domain-specific requirements the seeker never claims; graded down from any optimism about transferability. Task two: the only language requirement stated is good written and oral English ("Søkjarar må ha gode skriftlege og munnlege engelskkunnskapar") — the seeker says they speak Norwegian and says nothing about lacking English, and the ad imposes no Norwegian requirement. The clause about attachments being translated to English or a Scandinavian language concerns paperwork only (rule 4). No explicitly-stated deficiency of the seeker is required, so no violation.

The seeker is a carpenter (trade certificate, 10 years in new builds and renovation). The advertisement is for ventilation installers and asks for a trade certificate as ventilation and sheet metal worker or ~5 years' experience as a ventilation installer. Same broad construction sector and on-site work alongside other trades, but a different trade entirely from carpentry — the seeker would not apply and does not meet the stated trade requirements, so adjacent (1) rather than plausible (2). Graded down on uncertainty since the ad's requirements are trade-specific as written.

Task two: the only language clause is "The position requires the ability to communicate in English or Norwegian" — an either/or choice, so per rule 3 not a violation for a non-Norwegian speaker who can operate in English. The Class B licence is only "an advantage" and the seeker holds one anyway. No authorisation requirement stated. No violation.

Seeker is a certified carpenter (fagbrev) with ten years' experience in both new-build and rehabilitation; the ad seeks exactly that — carpenters with fagbrev or solid experience for nybygg and rehabilitering projects. Right occupation and level, so grade 3. Task two: the ad's stated requirements are a Scandinavian language ("Behersker et skandinavisk språk godt" — the seeker speaks Norwegian, satisfied) and a driving licence with access to a car ("Har førerkort og disponerer bil" — seeker has class B licence; the ad does not state a class the seeker lacks, and car access is not something the seeker said they lack). Våtromssertifikat is explicitly "gjerne", i.e. desirable not required. No violation of anything the seeker explicitly said they do not have.

Occupation match: the ad seeks experienced carpenters/installers, and the seeker is a carpenter with a trade certificate and ten years in new builds and renovation. The specialism (lightweight partition and glass wall installation, office interiors, possible drywall) is a carpentry niche the seeker has not named explicitly, but the ad's core requirement is "Experience as an Installer or Carpenter", which is squarely met, and general new-build/renovation carpentry ordinarily covers partition and interior work. Level is right (skilled tradesperson, not lead/supervisor). The required Category B driving licence is held. Some uncertainty exists on the 48-hour week, mobile project work and accommodation arrangement suiting the seeker's preferences, but the seeker stated no contrary preference, so this does not pull the grade down. Task two: the advertisement is silent on language — no Norwegian or English requirement appears anywhere in the text — so the seeker's lack of Norwegian is not a violation. No authorisation or licence requirement is unmet.

Seeker is a qualified primary/lower-secondary teacher (norsk and matematikk) seeking a permanent full position in the Oslo area from autumn. The advertisement is for cleaners (renholdere), a different occupation entirely — no overlap in field, competence or level. It also offers only 10-50% part-time posts, on-call and holiday cover, explicitly suited to someone wanting extra income, which is the opposite of the sought permanent post. Grade 0 on occupation alone; the location match (Oslo) is not enough to raise it. Task two: the only language clause is "Vi forventer at du kan kommunisere på norsk eller engelsk" / "Norsk eller engelsk" — the seeker writes in Norwegian and teaches Norwegian, so no language requirement is unmet. The stated competence requirement is cleaning experience, which the seeker never says she lacks, and the ad accepts someone "lærevillig" in any case. No authorisation or licence demanded. No violation.

The seeker is a backend developer (Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes) looking for a permanent position in Oslo or hybrid. The advertisement is for a waiter/extra help in food service (serving, cleaning, dishwashing, cash register) on an on-call basis — a completely different occupation, and also the wrong contract type. Grade 0. On task two: the ad requires fluent Norwegian ("Vi ser etter deg som snakker flytende norsk og som er effektiv"), but the seeker states they speak Norwegian ("Jeg snakker norsk"), so no requirement is violated. No authorisation or licence requirements are stated.

Seeker is a data scientist seeking AI/analytics roles; this is a senior data engineering role (pipelines, platforms, data products). Same field and shared skills (Python, SQL, ML-adjacent, works alongside data scientists), but a different specialism and a senior level the seeker's stated profile does not clearly reach — hence 2 rather than 3, recording the lower of an uncertain 2/1 boundary since the emphasis on years of pipeline-building experience is off-specialism. On language: the ad requires "Gode norsk- og engelskkunnskaper", and the seeker says she speaks Norwegian, so no violation; English is not addressed either way, and silence about her English is not evidence of a lack. The security clearance clause ("må kunne sikkerhetsklareres") is a condition she has not said she fails, so no authorisation violation.

Right occupation (authorised nurse), but two of the seeker's stated wants are explicitly contradicted as written: all posts are temporary cover positions ("100 % stilling vikariat sykepleier", "550 % stilling vikariat sykepleiere"), not permanent, and all are rotating shifts — "Alle våre stillinger er turnusstillinger, med arbeid på dag, kveld, natt og helg" — so no day-shift option. judgments.notes:

Right occupation (grunnskolelærer / teaching post) and the seeker's maths competence matches one of the wanted subjects. Du må kunne snakke, lese og skrive norsk..." but the seeker writes in Norwegian and is a Norwegian-qualified grunnskolelærer, so this requirement is met, not violated. Seeker wants warehouse work with a forklift certificate. Task two: the advertisement says nothing about Norwegian language ability (only that the company is Oslo-based and works with the Norwegian Armed Forces/FFI), so no language requirement is imposed; silence is not a violation. The mandatory "Trade certificate or DSB approval" is a licence requirement the seeker almost certainly lacks, but she never explicitly stated she lacks it — she simply said nothing about electrical trade credentials — so under the evidence rule no violation is recorded. The unsuitability here is captured by the relevance grade, not by a constraint breach.

A category B driving licence is required, but the seeker said nothing about lacking one, so that is not a violation of anything she explicitly stated she does not have. No Norwegian-language or authorisation requirement is imposed on her stated gaps.

This is a different occupation from data science/AI/analytics — no machine learning, Python, SQL or analytics content. The passing note that experience with AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude is an advantage is about using consumer AI tools for clerical work, not about building AI or analytics, so it does not lift this into the seeker's field. Grade 0.

Per rule 1, silence is not a violation, so no violated facet is recorded despite the Norwegian wording. No authorisation or licence requirement is stated either.

Right occupation (grunnskolelærer, 1.-7. trinn) and the seeker's teaching competence in norsk/matematikk matches one listed requirement. However, the ad as written also requires a master's degree in spesialpedagogikk and fordypning in a praktisk-estetisk subject, neither of which the seeker claims — a specialised special-education post rather than the general teaching role sought. The post is also in Trondheim kommune, while the seeker wants a permanent position in the Oslo area. Graded 2 (lower of uncertain options) on specialism and location mismatch; the ad says nothing about language, so no violation is recorded (silence is not a violation), and the seeker is a Norwegian speaker in any case.

Graded 1 rather than 2 since the seeker would be unlikely to apply. No language, authorisation or licence requirement in the ad that the seeker lacks — the only licence named, klasse B, the seeker holds; the ad is silent on language.

judgments.notes: The advertisement is for helsefagarbeider/hjelpepleier (healthcare assistant/auxiliary nurse), a lower qualification level than a registered nurse, and the stated qualification requirement is "Autorisasjon som helsefagarbeider/hjelpepleier" — not nursing authorisation. Right occupation (sykepleier) and right sector (sykehus), and the seeker has hospital experience. Right occupation and level: nurse role requiring Norwegian authorisation, which the seeker holds (autorisasjon + HPR-nummer). Graded 2 rather than 3 because the shift pattern is explicitly at odds with the seeker's stated preference for dagvakt — the ad emphasises evening and weekend shifts, often as sole nurse on duty — and the ad states neither the location (Trondheim not confirmed) nor that the position is permanent (fast stilling), both of which the seeker specified. "Gode norskkunnskaper" is not a violation for a seeker who wrote in Norwegian. Overlap is real but the core specialism is off. Contract type and location match well (permanent role, Statnett is Oslo-based, "Muligheten til å jobbe hjemmefra" supports hybrid). On task two: the language clause is "Flytende norsk er en fordel, eller vilje til å lære norsk, da norsk er arbeidsspråket i Statnett" — Norwegian is merely an advantage, and the seeker states "Jeg snakker norsk" anyway, so no violation. judgments.notes:
Teaching post at a school in Norway, so right occupation and sector.
